item.description: Background: Neurodegenerative diseases are a major and growing global health burden. Their pathogenesis is complex, and effective therapies remain limited. item.description: Background: The increasing number of older adults living with chronic conditions has led to rapid growth in information and communication technologies (ICTs) designed to support chronic disease self-management. item.description: Background: Postoperative sleep is closely associated with recovery among patients undergoing surgery. item.description: Background: Occupational e-mental health (OeMH) interventions emerged as a promising solution to prevent common mental health problems and enhance well-being and work performance. item.title: Mapping Digital Nudges and Recommender Systems for Obesity Prevention: Scoping Review
item.description: Background: Recommender systems are pivotal in organizing information to enhance noticeability, reduce overload, and streamline decision-making. They can be even more effective if combined with digital nudges. Digital nudging is a subtle approach that combines design, information, and interaction elements to create a choice architecture that can guide user behavior in digital environments. item.title: Evidence-Based Self-Management Strategies for Fibromyalgia: Foundations for Digital Therapeutic Applications
item.description: Fibromyalgia is a prevalent musculoskeletal pain condition that causes major personal, social, and societal burden. Pharmacological therapies often provide only limited benefit, making multimodal approaches and self-management the cornerstones of care. item.description: Background: Social isolation and loneliness have considerable health implications. item.description: Background: Aged care has recently undergone major transformations due to demographic aging and the concomitant need to manage health care costs. New emerging technologies (ETs) have started to play central roles in the daily management of older adults. item.title: Internet Use and Self-Rated Health Among Older Adults: Scoping Review
item.description: Background: Self-rated health (SRH) is a robust predictor of morbidity, functional decline, and mortality in later life.
